wording: In a transcritical bifurcation one equilibrium passes through another and they exchange stability: for dx/dt = r x - x^2 the equilibria are 0 and r, and at r = 0 they collide and swap stabilities, so for r > 0 the zero state becomes unstable and a new nonzero state takes over.
locator: P22 section 8.2, Eqs. 8.8-8.9 (read in full in DVC)
counterevidence_limits: One-variable normal form; reading it as 'insurgence' is this track's operationalization, not P22's term.
operationalization: NAT Insurgence = a new state rising when a threshold is crossed (exchange of stability)

wording: With noise sigma = 0.005 (larger than the seed 0.001) the transcritical onset at r = 0.05 came at 21.4 time units on average (SE 1.2) instead of the deterministic 77.8, with a coefficient of variation of 0.82; with sigma = 0.0005 the advance was not supported (76.8, SE 1.6), but onset timing still varied (CV 0.30). Noise makes the moment of onset unpredictable; it brings onset forward only when it is large relative to the seed.
counterevidence_limits: Reflecting boundary at x = 0 pushes small x upward, so part of the strong-noise advance is a boundary effect (disclosed in the SPEC).
operationalization: NAT Insurgence = onset timing under noise
